newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate rises 40 bps to 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate rises 40 bps to 11 pct.

text.p: Croatia's weighted money market rate climbed 40 basis points to 11 percent on Wednesday thanks to a slightly higher demand for term kuna funds.
Dealers put total trade at a low 24.4 million kuna, against 40 million on offer. Only 16.7 million kuna were fresh loans, of which 12 million call money loans at a stable 10.5 percent.
Other interbank loans were granted 12 and 13 percent. Old borrowings by savings banks were rolled over at a higher 14-20 percent, depending on term.
Insurers charged a steady 9.0 for renewed one-week deals.
The central bank stayed out of the foreign exchange market after last week's intervention, mostly to drain kuna liquidity.
Its kuna midrate for Thursday eased further to 5.8667 versus 5.8528 to the dollar but was little changed at 3.5638 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
